solutionSql:
SELECT to_char(s.booked_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM') AS booking_month,
       COUNT(*)::integer AS unbilled_shipments
FROM shipments AS s
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoices AS i WHERE i.shipment_id = s.id)
GROUP BY to_char(s.booked_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM')
ORDER BY booking_month;

ambiguities.phrase: For each UTC booking month ... count the shipments that have no invoice
ambiguities.readingChosen: List only months that have at least one unbilled shipment (anti-join, then group); a month whose shipments are all invoiced does not appear.
ambiguities.alternativeReading: List every month in which any shipment was booked, showing 0 for months where every shipment has an invoice (LEFT JOIN with COUNT FILTER or COUNT(i.id) inverted).

ambiguities.phrase: A shipment with an invoice is billed, whether or not the invoice is paid
ambiguities.readingChosen: Any invoice row for the shipment makes it billed; paid_at is ignored.
ambiguities.alternativeReading: None plausible; the sentence rules out treating unpaid invoices as unbilled.

notes: Anti-join with NOT EXISTS, month from booked_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' via to_char YYYY-MM, count cast to integer. Sample has no month with zero unbilled shipments, so both readings of month inclusion give the same sample rows; hidden data could separate them. Invoices are at most one per shipment, so no duplication risk either way.
